chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding His Exalted Saying: 'Let two just men from among you judge' (Quran 65:2)
The 'just one' is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam after him; he is the one with justice.
So when you know what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imam have judged, that is sufficient for you, and do not ask about it.
ai.seo_question: Who is the 'just one' (al-'Adl) referred to in the Quranic verse about judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* offers a Shia exegetical interpretation of Surah At-Talaq 65:2, identifying the 'just one' (al-'Adl) as the Prophet Muhammad and the subsequent Imam, thereby linking judicial authority to divine infallibility. It establishes that the rulings of the Prophet and the Imam are definitive and sufficient, advising believers to accept their judgment without excessive questioning, which underscores the concept of *Tawqif* (divine specification) in Shia jurisprudence.
